# DevEco-OAuth

[![CI](https://github.com/WangHui-code/DevEco-OAuth/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/WangHui-code/DevEco-OAuth/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-informational.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![Node.js ≥ 20](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-339933.svg)](https://nodejs.org/)

**[English](./README.md)** | 简体中文

**用你的华为账号，在 opencode 与 Claude Code 里直接使用 DevEco Code 的模型（`GLM-5.1-DevEco` / `GLM-5.3-DevEco`）。**

> **非官方项目。** 与华为无关联、未获华为认可或赞助。"DevEco"、"DevEco Studio"、"HarmonyOS" 是华为技术有限公司的商标，此处仅为描述兼容性而引用。

DevEco Code 的模型此前只能在 DevEco Studio 里用。本项目把它接进你日常的终端编码工具：opencode **2.x** 有原生进程内插件（`opencode auth login` 一条命令完成登录，凭证由 opencode 托管、自动刷新）；opencode **1.x** 与 Claude Code 走本地代理（OpenAI / Anthropic 双协议端点）；其他 OpenAI 兼容客户端同样可以接入。

> ⚠️ 仅支持中国大陆站点（`siteId=1`）的华为账号，与上游 DevEco Code 一致；推理需完成华为实名认证。

---

## 特性

- **华为账号 OAuth 登录，长期免登** —— 浏览器一键授权；30 分钟 access token 静默刷新，重启进程免登，jwtToken 以天/周计
- **OpenAI + Anthropic 双协议** —— `/v2/chat/completions` 与 `/anthropic/v1/messages`，Claude Code 直接可用；流式、工具调用、thinking、图片全支持
- **opencode 2.x 原生插件** —— 进程内注册 OAuth 集成域，`opencode auth login` 选择 DevEco Code 即登录；凭证存进 opencode 的凭证库（SQLite，跨进程共享），到期前约 5 分钟自动刷新，上游 `401` 强制刷新并重试
- **识图自动路由** —— 文本模型收到带图请求自动转发视觉模型，下一轮自动切回，客户端无感
- **思考流分离** —— GLM 的自言自语走独立通道（`reasoning_content` / `thinking` block），不污染正文；`GLM-5.3-DevEco` 的 low/high/max 档位可切换
- **长会话稳定** —— Chat-Id 锚定对话首条用户消息，system 提示词每轮变化也不会反复新开上游会话；每轮结束释放服务端队列槽位
- **排队与并发控制** —— 默认串行、有界队列、入场冷却：突发请求排队而不是撞 DevEco 按账号限流，超出上限 `429` 快速失败
- **模型目录** —— `/v2/models` 提供云端模型列表（每小时刷新、静态兜底、含上下文长度）；加载插件 `config` hook 的构建会把它注入 opencode（含档位与模态），2.x 插件则以静态目录注册两个 GLM 模型及其档位变体（磁盘上的云端目录优先于内置兜底）；`deepseek-v4-flash` 等隐藏模型可手工启用
- **企业代理友好** —— 登录、刷新、模型列表、推理全链路读取 `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY`
- **无头服务器可登录** —— SSH 隧道完成浏览器 OAuth；`/v2/login`、`/v2/status` 对脚本友好
- **数据实测** —— needle-in-haystack 实测各模型真实可用上下文（GLM-5.x ≈200K；`deepseek-v4-flash` 硬上限 1,044,480 tokens）

## 接入路径

| 你的客户端 | 接入方式 | 登录方式 |
|---|---|---|
| opencode **2.x** | 原生进程内插件，无需代理 | `opencode auth login` → 选择 DevEco Code |
| opencode **1.x**（已验证 1.17.6 / 1.18.x / 1.19.6） | 本地代理，OpenAI 兼容端点 | 浏览器打开 `/v2/login` |
| [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) | 本地代理的 `/anthropic` 端点 | 浏览器打开 `/v2/login` |
| 其他 OpenAI 兼容客户端 | 本地代理的 `/v2` 端点 | 浏览器打开 `/v2/login` |

---

## 快速开始

前置条件：Node 20+；中国大陆站点华为账号（推理需完成实名认证）。

### opencode 2.x（原生插件）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WangHui-code/DevEco-OAuth.git
cd DevEco-OAuth
npm install
npm run build

# 注册进 opencode 2.x 的全局插件目录（一次性）
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins
ln -s "$PWD" ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-deveco

# 浏览器登录华为账号
opencode auth login     # 选择 DevEco Code
```

之后在 opencode 里选择 `deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco` 或 `deveco/GLM-5.3-DevEco` 即可。

- 凭证由 opencode 框架托管：SQLite 持久化、跨进程共享，到期前自动刷新；上游返回 `401` 时插件强制刷新并重试。
- 插件在进程内直接转发，无需常驻代理。调试时可以跳过登录：设置 `DEVECO_ACCESS_TOKEN`（30 分钟有效）。
- 验收：`npm run test:e2e`（本地 mock 上游 + 真实 `opencode acp`，断言 Bearer 注入、Chat-Id、模型 id 改写、每个 chat 轮次的规范化怪癖、exitSessionQueue 等全部网关行为，无需华为账号）；`npm run test:e2e:proxy`（1.x 本地代理链路，需用 `OPENCODE_BIN` 指向 opencode 1.x）；`npm run test:e2e:real`（真实上游，需先 `opencode auth login`）。
- 若通过 ACP 宿主使用：ACP 的 authenticate 目前是 stub，登录入口不可用，请在终端运行 `opencode auth login`。

### opencode 1.x 与 Claude Code（本地代理）

opencode 1.x 的发布二进制不加载外部插件的 auth hooks，无法通过插件系统注入 DevEco 的 Bearer token。因此走一个本地小代理：opencode 把它当作普通 OpenAI 端点访问，代理负责登录、token 刷新与转发。

```
opencode  ──►  http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2  （本代理）
                     │  + 注入 Authorization: Bearer <devEco token>
                     │  + 应用 DevEco /no-stream URL 规则
                     ▼
              https://cn.devecostudio.huawei.com/sse/codeGenie/maas/v2
```

已在 opencode `1.17.6` / `1.18.x` 上对接真实上游端到端验证通过，并在 `1.19.6` 上通过 mock 上游验收脚本（`npm run test:e2e:proxy`）。插件（`src/plugin.ts`）负责启动代理，并在加载外部插件 `config` hook 的构建上注入 `deveco` provider；auth hook 兜底路径已移除（已发布的 1.x 都不加载外部 auth hook），所以代理仍是实际路径。

#### 1. 安装

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WangHui-code/DevEco-OAuth.git
cd DevEco-OAuth
npm install            # 安装构建依赖
npm run build          # 生成 dist/
npm run test           # 运行测试
```

构建产物是 `dist/proxy.js`（代理入口）与 `scripts/`（各平台自启动脚本）。

#### 2. 让 opencode 指向代理

在 `opencode.json` 里加一个 `deveco` provider，`baseURL` 指向本地代理。`apiKey` 是占位符 —— 真实 token 由代理注入。

```jsonc
{
  "provider": {
    "deveco": {
      "name": "DevEco Code",
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2",
        "apiKey": "opencode-oauth-dummy-key"
      },
      "models": {
        "GLM-5.1-DevEco": {
          "name": "GLM-5.1-DevEco",
          "reasoning": true,
          "tool_call": true,
          "limit": { "context": 170000, "output": 32000 },
          "modalities": { "input": ["text"], "output": ["text"] }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> 小贴士：如果你的 opencode 构建会加载外部插件的 `config` hook，把 `"opencode-deveco"` 加到 `plugin` 数组里即可 —— 它会自动启动代理并注入上面的 provider 配置。

#### 3. 启动代理

代理默认监听 `127.0.0.1:17128`。用 `DEVECO_PROXY_PORT=<端口>` 覆盖（并同步修改第 2 步的 `baseURL`）。

**前台运行**（首次运行 / 调试首选 —— 日志实时打印到终端）：

```bash
node dist/proxy.js
```

**带守护进程运行（推荐）** —— `npm start` 在监督进程 `dist/daemon.js` 下运行代理，代理意外退出时自动重启（退避 1s → 2s → … → 最长 30s，稳定运行超过 60s 后退避重置），Ctrl+C 会一并停止两者。不需要守护时用 `npm run start:proxy` 直接跑代理。

```bash
npm start                     # 守护 + 代理（前台，日志到终端）
npm start -- --port=17129     # 参数会透传给代理
```

**Windows —— 隐藏窗口后台进程**（无任务栏窗口；日志写入 `proxy.log`；同样带守护）：

```powershell
# 在项目根目录执行
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\start-windows.ps1
# 停止（会先杀守护进程再杀代理）：
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\stop-windows.ps1
# 不要守护时：
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\start-windows.ps1 -NoWatchdog
```

> 开机自启：用任务计划程序（或在「启动」文件夹放一个快捷方式）运行 `start-windows.ps1`。

**Linux / macOS —— 后台进程：**

```bash
nohup node dist/proxy.js > proxy.log 2>&1 &
```

**Linux —— systemd 用户服务（自启 + 自动重启）：**

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp scripts/opencode-deveco.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
# 编辑复制后的文件里的 ExecStart / WorkingDirectory 为你的实际安装路径
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now opencode-deveco
journalctl --user -u opencode-deveco -f   # 实时看日志
```

> 这个 systemd unit 在用户登录时自启。要实现开机自启（登录前就启动）运行 `loginctl enable-linger $USER`。systemd 自身就会重启进程（`Restart=on-failure`），所以这里继续直接运行 `dist/proxy.js`，不必再套一层 `daemon.js`。

**macOS —— launchd 用户代理（自启 + 自动重启）：**

```bash
mkdir -p ~/Library/LaunchAgents
cp scripts/com.opencode-deveco.proxy.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
# 编辑复制后的文件里的 node / 项目 / 日志路径
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.opencode-deveco.proxy.plist
tail -f ~/Library/Logs/opencode-deveco.log   # 实时看日志
# 停止：launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.opencode-deveco.proxy
```

> 必须用 LaunchAgent 而不是 LaunchDaemon —— agent 跑在你已登录的图形会话里，自动打开浏览器登录才能生效。launchd 不读 shell 配置且 `PATH` 极简，所以 plist 里要写 `node` 的绝对路径（用 `which node` 查）。launchd 自带 KeepAlive 重启，无需再套 `daemon.js`。

#### 4. 登录

**用浏览器**打开 `http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login`，会直接 302 跳到华为 OAuth 页面。该端点立即返回、不再挂住连接等回调，所以脚本调用拿到的是登录 URL：

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login
# → {"login_url":"https://cn.devecostudio.huawei.com/console/DevEcoIDE/apply?port=10101&..."}
curl http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/status   # 轮询直到 {"logged_in":true,...}
```

未登录时发请求，代理会尝试替你打开浏览器，并给这次请求返回 `401` + 同一个登录 URL —— 登录完成后重试即可。（作为后台服务运行且没有桌面会话时，自动打开无法生效，用 `401` 或 `/v2/login` 返回的 URL 手动登录。）

##### 在无头服务器上登录

华为会把浏览器重定向回 `http://127.0.0.1:<端口>/callback`，而这个监听只绑 loopback —— 浏览器和它必须共享同一个 localhost。用 SSH 隧道把两者接起来：

```bash
# 在桌面机器上执行，整个登录过程保持会话开着
ssh -L 10101:127.0.0.1:10101 -L 17128:127.0.0.1:17128 user@server
```

然后用桌面机器的浏览器打开 `http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login` 完成登录，回调会经隧道送达服务器，凭证落在服务器上。

> 回调端口不一定是 10101 —— 被占用时会依次退到 34567-34570。按登录 URL 里 `port=` 给出的端口转发。

两个端口都只绑 loopback，代理自身也不做任何鉴权，所以走隧道是有意为之的访问方式，不要直接把端口暴露出去。

#### 5. 验证

```bash
opencode models                                # 应能看到 deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco 和 deveco/GLM-5.3-DevEco
opencode run "say hi" -m deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco # 通过代理发真实请求
```

> 对外模型 id 是 **`GLM-5.1-DevEco` / `GLM-5.3-DevEco`** —— 华为部署的版本，不是智谱公版。代理仍兼容旧的裸 id（`GLM-5.1` / `GLM-5.3`），但模型列表和文档统一用 `-DevEco` 名字。如果看到 `ProviderModelNotFoundError` 且 `suggestions: ["GLM-5.1-DevEco"]`，改成该名字即可。

### Claude Code

代理同时支持 **Anthropic Messages API**（`POST /anthropic/v1/messages`），自动将请求转换为 OpenAI Chat Completions 格式，让 Claude Code 直接使用 DevEco 模型。启动前设置：

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:17128/anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=opencode-oauth-dummy-key
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL=GLM-5.1-DevEco
```

流式传输、工具调用、thinking 块和图片内容都支持。

---

## 模型

DevEco 渠道提供的是昇腾量化部署版本，不是智谱公版权重。两个 ModelScope 模型卡的情况：

| 对外模型 | 渠道模型 | 参数量 | 权重体积 | 量化 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `GLM-5.3-DevEco` | [`Eco-Tech/GLM-5.3-w8a8c8`](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/GLM-5.3-w8a8c8) | 755.71B | 约 764 GB | W8A8C8：INT8 权重（per-channel）、INT8 激活（per-token 动态）、INT8 KV Cache（per-tile 128） |
| `GLM-5.1-DevEco` | [`Eco-Tech/GLM-5.1-w4a8`](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/GLM-5.1-w4a8) | 395.82B | 约 420 GB | W4A8（模型卡未展开具体量化配置） |

- 两者都是昇腾部署：GLM-5.3 用 msModelSlim + QuaRot，在 Atlas A2/A3 上通过 vLLM-Ascend 验证；GLM-5.1 在 Atlas 800T A3 上通过 vLLM-Ascend 验证。
- 两个 ModelScope 仓库都是 MIT License；基座模型许可单独适用：GLM-5.3 原始权重遵循 ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3 仓库条款，GLM-5.1 基座来自 `zai-org/GLM-5.1`。
- 模型卡没有给出该渠道的上下文/最大输出声明；本 README 的 170,000 / 32,000 来自 DevEco 的 `modelConfig`，不是模型卡。
- GLM-5.1 模型卡给出 GPQA 87.3（官方 86.2）；GLM-5.3 模型卡的精度与部署章节仍标注「待补充」。

> 渠道当前声明 `GLM-5.1-DevEco` / `GLM-5.3-DevEco` 均为 **170,000 context / 32,000 最大输出**。这与智谱官方规格不同（官方 5.1 为 200K/131K，5.3 为 1M/131K）；代理的静态兜底与示例配置按渠道值写入，超过 32K 的 `max_tokens` 会被压到 32K。

### 上下文长度实测（2026-09-17）

用 **needle-in-haystack** 探针实测各模型真实可用的上下文：把随机暗号埋在长文约 30% 处、要求原样回读，并以响应里的 `usage.prompt_tokens`（上游真实计数）为准，从约 2.5K tokens 起逐级放大：

| 模型 | 上游声明 `context_window` | 实测通过 | 实测被拒 | 结论 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | 未声明（不在模型表中） | 1,042,769 tokens（约 85 s） | 1,044,994 → `400 OverLimitRequestBody` | 硬上限 **1,044,480** tokens（≈1020K） |
| `GLM-5.3-DevEco`（上游 `GLM-5.3`） | 170,000 | 198,197 tokens（116 s） | 209,880 → `403 ModelServiceError` | 有效 **≈200K** |
| `GLM-5.1-DevEco`（上游 `GLM-5.1`） | 170,000 | 198,192 tokens（49 s） | 204,110 → `403 ModelServiceError` | 有效 **≈200K** |

- **`deepseek-v4-flash` 是明确的硬限制**，上游报错会直接给出数字：`the prompt length 1044994 must less than the maximum input length 1044480`。超限即 `400`，边界干净。
- **GLM-5.x 的拒绝不是长度报错**，而是 `403 ModelServiceError`：`Built-in model service is currently overloaded` / `Full inference timed out`（约 35 s 快速拒绝，不是真的跑满超时）。198K 稳定通过、204K 起稳定被拒，所以 ≈200K 是**观测量**而不是上游声明；实际使用建议留余量（`GLM-5.1-DevEco` 按 ~190K、`GLM-5.3-DevEco` 按 ~180K 更稳，后者在 198K 时单次要 116 s）。
- 同一段文本 GLM 的分词更省（约 1.17 tokens/词 vs deepseek 的 1.23），但可用容量仍差一个数量级。
- 压测期间代理**未崩溃**：单请求 body 约 4 MB、连续 50+ 次调用都拿到正常 HTTP 响应；唯一一次 5xx 是并行发两个大请求时上游断连（`upstream fetch failed`），代理返回 `500` 后继续服务。
- 复现方法：以 `usage.prompt_tokens` 为准从 2K 起按约 1.25 倍递增，直到被拒；把暗号挪到接近结尾（如 90% 处）可额外验证尾部是否被完整读取。

### 隐藏模型 `deepseek-v4-flash`

它既不在 `GET /v2/models`，也不在上游 `modelConfig` 里。靠模型列表自动拉取的客户端看不到它，必须手写模型名。代理对模型名不做限制，上游认识的 id 直接指定即可；它的元数据（上下文/模态/档位）上游一概不提供。需要时手工启用（以 opencode 为例，写进 `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`）：

```json
"provider": {
  "deveco": {
    "models": {
      "deepseek-v4-flash": {
        "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash (1M)",
        "limit": { "context": 1044480, "output": 32000 }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`context` 用上面的实测硬上限；`output` 上游未声明，此处按 GLM 同级取 32000。它的思考天然走 `reasoning_content`（无需任何参数），与 GLM 需要 `enable_thinking` 才分离不同。

## 行为细节

### 识图自动路由（文本模型的视觉补充）

`GLM-5.1-DevEco` / `GLM-5.3-DevEco` 都是文本模型，带图片的请求会被上游拒绝（HTTP 403）。代理内置**透明识图转发**，无需修改 opencode 配置：

- **哪些模型算「文本-only」由上游模型配置自动判定**：代理读取 `modelConfig` 返回的 `input_modalities`，只声明 `["text"]` 的模型即视为文本模型（随模型列表缓存 1 小时）。上游新增模型或调整能力时无需改代码；模型配置不可用（冷启动、离线、未登录）时回退内置列表 `GLM-5.1,GLM-5.3`（上游 id）。
- 请求模型是文本-only、且**最新一条用户消息含图片**时，代理自动改用视觉模型 `Qwen3_5_397B_A17B_w8a8_single` 转发，响应原样返回，客户端无感知。
- 下一轮没有新图片时自动回到原模型；历史消息里的旧图片会被替换为 `[图片]` 占位符（上轮视觉模型得出的文字结论仍在历史里），避免文本模型再次报 403。
- 转发到视觉模型时会移除 `tools` / `tool_choice` —— 该模型不输出结构化工具调用，直接以文字描述图片。
- OpenAI 端点与 Anthropic 端点都适用，流式/非流式都支持。

日志中可看到路由动作：

```
-> POST no-stream model=GLM-5.1-DevEco → vision:Qwen3_5_397B_A17B_w8a8_single
```

### 会话稳定性（避免「几轮后无响应」）

DevEco 对短时间新建会话数量有限制（`UserSessionLimitExceeded`）。代理默认只用**第一条用户消息**作为会话 key（Chat-Id），因此 Claude Code 的 system 提示词即使每轮变化（日期、目录等动态内容），对话仍复用同一 Chat-Id，不会触发新建会话限流。

- 客户端可显式传 `x-session-id` / `x-deveco-session` / `x-session-affinity` 头，优先级最高；
- 需要恢复「system + 首条消息」的旧语义时，设置 `DEVECO_SESSION_KEY_MODE=system-first`。

### 并发与排队

- `DEVECO_MAX_CONCURRENCY`（默认 `1`）限制同时在跑的上游生成回合数，突发请求按到达顺序排队，而不是去撞 DevEco 的按账号限流。
- 排队请求放行前冷却 `DEVECO_QUEUE_COOLDOWN_SEC`（默认 `1`，可小数如 `0.5`；设 `0` 关闭）；直接拿到空闲槽位的请求立即发出，冷却中的槽位保留给该排队者，后来者不能插队。
- 队列上限 `DEVECO_MAX_QUEUE`（默认 `3`）：再多直接回 `429`（`rate_limit_error`），不会在长回合后面堆成无限积压；设 `0` 表示不排队。
- 一轮结束后，等 DevEco 确认服务端队列槽位已释放（`exitSessionQueue`，等待上限 3 秒）才把槽位交给下一个排队回合。元数据接口（`/v2/status`、`/v2/models`、`/v2/login`、`/v2/logout`）完全不排队。

| 变量 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `DEVECO_PROXY_PORT` | `17128` | 代理监听端口；修改后同步更新 provider 的 `baseURL` |
| `DEVECO_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | 日志级别：`debug` / `info` / `warn` / `error` |
| `DEVECO_VISION_MODEL` | `Qwen3_5_397B_A17B_w8a8_single` | 识图兜底模型 |
| `DEVECO_TEXT_ONLY_MODELS` | 自动（按上游 `input_modalities`） | 视为纯文本的模型，逗号分隔；显式设置时以此为准，模型配置不可用时回退内置 `GLM-5.1,GLM-5.3` |
| `DEVECO_SESSION_KEY_MODE` | 首条用户消息 | 设为 `system-first` 恢复「system + 首条消息」的旧会话 key 语义 |

## 日志与可观测性

代理把日志打到 stdout（info）和 stderr（warn/error）—— 前台运行就在终端，后台就在你重定向的文件里。每个请求产生一对日志：

```
[2026-06-14T16:53:24.999Z] [INFO] -> POST stream model=GLM-5.1-DevEco
[2026-06-14T16:53:27.150Z] [INFO] <- 200 2151ms in=2677 out=7 model=GLM-5.1-DevEco (backend: GLM5_1_W4A8-1.0.0)
```

`in=`/`out=` 是输入与输出 token 数，末尾 `backend:` 是 DevEco 实际调度的模型。token 刷新、`401` 重试、登录等会话事件也会记录。

通过 `DEVECO_LOG_LEVEL` 控制详细程度（默认 `info`）。

> opencode 自己的日志（`~/.local/share/opencode/log/`）只能看到请求打到 `http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2`，看不到 DevEco 侧细节。代理日志才是 DevEco 真实调用链路所在。

## Token 存储与刷新

| 凭证 | 位置 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `accessToken`（30 分钟） | 代理内存中 | 下次请求自动刷新 |
| `jwtToken`（长效刷新凭证） | `~/.config/opencode/opencode-deveco/jwt.json` | 明文 JSON，`0600`；用 `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` 覆盖目录 |
| 国家/地区（非凭证） | `~/.config/deveco/country.region.xml` | 登录成功后写入，供 DevEco Studio 共用；原子写，失败只记日志 |

### token 过期 / 重启机器后需要重新登录吗？

**绝大多数情况都不需要** —— 只有当长效 `jwtToken` 本身失效（通常以天/周计）时才需要重新走浏览器登录。三种情况：

| 场景 | 需要重新登录？ | 实际发生的事 |
|---|---|---|
| `accessToken` 过期（每 30 分钟） | ❌ 不需要 | 代理用本地 jwtToken **静默刷新**，无浏览器、无操作。还有第二道保险：请求中被 DevEco 返回 `401` 时，代理会再刷新一次并重试。 |
| 重启机器 / 重启代理 | ❌ 不需要 | 代理启动时读取 `jwt.json` 并刷新恢复会话（`GET /v2/status` → `logged_in:true`），全程无头。你只需**重新启动代理进程**；建议加入系统开机自启。 |
| jwtToken 也失效 | ⚠️ 才需要 | 当长效 jwtToken 在服务端不再有效时，刷新会失败。此时下次请求会自动触发浏览器登录，或手动执行 `curl http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login`。 |

代理启动时会尝试用已存的 jwtToken 恢复会话（启动即刷新）。失败则等下次请求触发浏览器登录。

## 限制

- **仅中国大陆站**。非 CN 的 `siteId` 会被拒绝；非中国区账号在登录时就被拒，未实名账号在推理前会提示完成华为实名认证。
- **1.x 代理必须常驻运行**，opencode 1.x 才能访问 DevEco（其已发布二进制不加载外部插件 auth hook）。建议做成后台服务 / 开机自启。2.x 插件不需要代理。
- **jwtToken 明文存储**（不加密）。如需加密，把 `JsonTokenStore` 换成加密实现即可，只改 `token-store.ts`。
- **同一账号只能跑一个代理实例**。共用同一份 `jwt.json` 的第二个进程刷新必定失败（DevEco 似乎会在一次刷新成功后使先前的刷新凭据失效），只能退回浏览器登录。
- **默认端口 17128**，opencode 侧无法直接配置；通过 `DEVECO_PROXY_PORT` 改并同步更新 provider 的 `baseURL`。

## 故障排查

- **`opencode run ... -m deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco` 报连接被拒** → 代理没在跑。启动它（`node dist/proxy.js`）。
- **第一次请求弹了浏览器并返回 `401`** → 未登录时的正常表现：代理在后台发起登录，而不是让你干等。完成华为登录后重试即可；之后 30 分钟内都是无头的。
- **过一阵返回 `401`** → access token 过期且刷新失败（jwtToken 在服务端已失效）。再访问一次 `/v2/login`。
- **长回复中途报 `Upstream stream ended early`** → DevEco 在生成过程中沉默超过 120 秒。重试即可；若反复出现，多半是对话已超出模型上下文，需要压缩历史。
- **`opencode models` 没有 deveco 模型** → 检查 `opencode.json` 里有没有 `provider.deveco` 条目（这是配置驱动，不是插件驱动）。
- **非流式请求超时** → DevEco 的 `/no-stream` 接口可能较慢；请求体显式加 `"stream": true` 切回流式。代理默认以非流式转发 OpenAI 请求（仅显式 `stream: true` 才启用 SSE）；opencode 恒发 `stream: true`，不受影响。

## Features

- **Huawei-account OAuth, sign in once** — one-click browser authorization; the 30-minute access token refreshes silently, restarts need no re-login, and the long-lived jwtToken lasts days/weeks
- **OpenAI + Anthropic through one proxy** — `/v2/chat/completions` and `/anthropic/v1/messages`; Claude Code drops in directly, with streaming, tool calls, thinking blocks and images
- **Native opencode 2.x plugin** — registers an OAuth integration in-process; `opencode auth login` → DevEco Code; credentials live in opencode's store (SQLite, cross-process), refresh about 5 minutes before expiry, and an upstream `401` triggers a forced refresh and retry
- **Automatic vision routing** — a text model that receives an image is transparently re-routed to a vision model, and back again on the next turn
- **Reasoning kept out of the answer** — GLM's scratchpad travels on `reasoning_content` / `thinking` blocks instead of the reply; `GLM-5.3-DevEco` exposes low/high/max tiers
- **Stable long conversations** — the Chat-Id is pinned to the conversation's first user message, so a volatile system prompt can't mint a new upstream session every turn; the server queue slot is released each turn
- **Queueing and concurrency control** — serial by default, bounded queue, admission cooldown: bursts queue up instead of tripping DevEco's per-account throttle, and overflow fails fast with `429`
- **Model catalog** — `/v2/models` serves the cloud model list (hourly refresh, static fallback, context limits included); builds that load plugin `config` hooks get it injected into opencode (tiers and modalities included), while the 2.x plugin registers the two GLM models statically with their tier variants (the persisted cloud catalog wins over the built-in fallback); hidden models such as `deepseek-v4-flash` can be enabled by hand
- **Corporate-proxy friendly** — login, token refresh, model list and inference all honour `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY`
- **Headless login** — complete browser OAuth through an SSH tunnel; `/v2/login` and `/v2/status` are script-friendly
- **Measured, not guessed** — needle-in-haystack probes for the real usable context of each model (GLM-5.x ≈200K; `deepseek-v4-flash` hard cap 1,044,480 tokens)

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Node 20+; a China-site Huawei account (real-name verified for inference).

### opencode 2.x (native plugin)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WangHui-code/DevEco-OAuth.git
cd DevEco-OAuth
npm install
npm run build

# Register with opencode 2.x's global plugin directory (once)
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins
ln -s "$PWD" ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-deveco

# Sign in with your Huawei account in the browser
opencode auth login     # choose DevEco Code
```

Then pick `deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco` or `deveco/GLM-5.3-DevEco` in opencode.

- Credentials are owned by the opencode framework: SQLite-backed and cross-process, refreshed automatically before expiry; an upstream `401` makes the plugin force a refresh and retry.
- The plugin forwards in-process — no daemon proxy needed. For debugging you can skip login by setting `DEVECO_ACCESS_TOKEN` (valid for 30 minutes).
- Acceptance: `npm run test:e2e` (local mock upstream + real `opencode acp`; asserts Bearer injection, Chat-Id, model-id rewrite, the normalisation quirks on every chat turn, exitSessionQueue and the rest of the gateway contract — no Huawei account needed); `npm run test:e2e:proxy` (1.x local proxy path, needs an opencode 1.x `OPENCODE_BIN`); `npm run test:e2e:real` (real upstream; run `opencode auth login` first).
- Under an ACP host: ACP's authenticate is a stub, so the login entry is unavailable — run `opencode auth login` in a terminal.

### opencode 1.x and Claude Code (local proxy)

opencode 1.x's published binary does not load external plugins' auth hooks, so we can't inject DevEco's Bearer token through the plugin system. Instead this project runs a small local proxy that opencode talks to like any OpenAI endpoint: the proxy handles login, token refresh and forwarding.

```
opencode  ──►  http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2  (this proxy)
                     │  + injects Authorization: Bearer <devEco token>
                     │  + applies DevEco /no-stream URL rule
                     ▼
              https://cn.devecostudio.huawei.com/sse/codeGenie/maas/v2
```

Verified end-to-end against opencode `1.17.6` / `1.18.x` with the real upstream, and `1.19.6` against the mock-upstream harness (`npm run test:e2e:proxy`). The opencode plugin (`src/plugin.ts`) starts the proxy and injects the `deveco` provider on builds that load external plugin `config` hooks; the auth-hook fallback was removed because no released 1.x loads external auth hooks, so the proxy remains the working path.

#### 1. Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WangHui-code/DevEco-OAuth.git
cd DevEco-OAuth
npm install            # build dependencies
npm run build          # produces dist/
npm run test           # run tests
```

The build yields `dist/proxy.js` (the proxy entry point) and a `scripts/` folder with the OS autostart files.

#### 2. Point opencode at the proxy

Add a `deveco` provider to your `opencode.json` whose `baseURL` is the local proxy. The `apiKey` is a placeholder — the proxy injects the real token.

```jsonc
{
  "provider": {
    "deveco": {
      "name": "DevEco Code",
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2",
        "apiKey": "opencode-oauth-dummy-key"
      },
      "models": {
        "GLM-5.1-DevEco": {
          "name": "GLM-5.1-DevEco",
          "reasoning": true,
          "tool_call": true,
          "limit": { "context": 170000, "output": 32000 },
          "modalities": { "input": ["text"], "output": ["text"] }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> Tip: on opencode builds that load external plugin `config` hooks, also add `"opencode-deveco"` to the `plugin` array — it will start the proxy for you and inject the provider above automatically.

#### 3. Start the proxy

The proxy listens on `127.0.0.1:17128` by default. Override with `DEVECO_PROXY_PORT=<port>` (and update the `baseURL` in step 2 to match).

**Foreground** (best for first-run / debugging — logs print live to the terminal):

```bash
node dist/proxy.js
```

**Supervised (recommended)** — `npm start` runs the proxy under the supervisor `dist/daemon.js`, which relaunches it whenever it exits (backoff 1s → 2s → … capped at 30s, reset after a run that survived 60s). Ctrl+C stops both. Use `npm run start:proxy` to run the proxy alone.

```bash
npm start                     # supervisor + proxy (foreground, logs to terminal)
npm start -- --port=17129     # arguments are passed through to the proxy
```

**Windows — hidden background process** (no taskbar window; logs → `proxy.log`; supervised as well):

```powershell
# from the project root
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\start-windows.ps1
# stop it later (kills the supervisor first, then the proxy):
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\stop-windows.ps1
# without the watchdog:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\start-windows.ps1 -NoWatchdog
```

> For autostart on login: create a Task Scheduler task (or a shortcut in the Startup folder) that runs the `start-windows.ps1` script.

**Linux / macOS — background process:**

```bash
nohup node dist/proxy.js > proxy.log 2>&1 &
```

**Linux — systemd user service (autostart + auto-restart):**

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp scripts/opencode-deveco.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
# edit ExecStart / WorkingDirectory in the copied file to your install path
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now opencode-deveco
journalctl --user -u opencode-deveco -f   # follow logs
```

> The systemd unit enables lingering-free autostart on login. For boot-time autostart (before login) run `loginctl enable-linger $USER`. systemd already restarts the process (`Restart=on-failure`), so keep running `dist/proxy.js` here — no need to stack `daemon.js` on top.

**macOS — launchd user agent (autostart + auto-restart):**

```bash
mkdir -p ~/Library/LaunchAgents
cp scripts/com.opencode-deveco.proxy.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
# edit the node / project / log paths in the copied file
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.opencode-deveco.proxy.plist
tail -f ~/Library/Logs/opencode-deveco.log   # follow logs
# stop: launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.opencode-deveco.proxy
```

> Keep it a LaunchAgent rather than a LaunchDaemon — agents run inside your logged-in GUI session, which is what lets the automatic browser login work. launchd starts with a bare `PATH` and never reads your shell profile, so the plist needs the absolute path to `node` (`which node`). launchd's own KeepAlive covers restarts — no need to stack `daemon.js` on top.

#### 4. Log in

Open `http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login` **in a browser** — it redirects straight to the Huawei OAuth page. It returns immediately (302) rather than holding the connection open, so from a script you get the URL back instead:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login
# → {"login_url":"https://cn.devecostudio.huawei.com/console/DevEcoIDE/apply?port=10101&..."}
curl http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/status   # poll until {"logged_in":true,...}
```

If you send a request while logged out, the proxy tries to open a browser for you and answers that request with `401` plus the same login URL — complete the sign-in, then retry. (Running as a background service with no desktop session, the automatic open can't work; use the URL from the `401` or from `/v2/login`.)

##### Logging in on a headless server

Huawei sends the browser back to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`, and that listener binds loopback only — so the browser and the listener need a shared localhost. An SSH tunnel gives them one:

```bash
# from your desktop; keep it open for the whole login
ssh -L 10101:127.0.0.1:10101 -L 17128:127.0.0.1:17128 user@server
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login` in your desktop browser and sign in; the callback travels down the tunnel and the credentials land on the server.

> The callback port is not always 10101 — it falls back to 34567-34570 when taken. Forward whichever port the login URL's `port=` names.

Both ports bind loopback and the proxy has no authentication of its own, so a tunnel is the intended way in — don't expose the port instead.

#### 5. Verify

```bash
opencode models                                # should list deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco and deveco/GLM-5.3-DevEco
opencode run "say hi" -m deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco # real request through the proxy
```

> The exposed ids are **`GLM-5.1-DevEco` / `GLM-5.3-DevEco`** — Huawei's deployed variants, not the public Zhipu models. The proxy accepts the old bare ids (`GLM-5.1` / `GLM-5.3`) for compatibility, but the model list and docs use the `-DevEco` names. If you see `ProviderModelNotFoundError` with `suggestions: ["GLM-5.1-DevEco"]`, switch to that name.

## Models

The DevEco channel serves Ascend-quantized deployments, not the public Zhipu checkpoints. The ModelScope cards describe the two versions:

| Exposed id | Channel model | Params | Weights | Quantization |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `GLM-5.3-DevEco` | [`Eco-Tech/GLM-5.3-w8a8c8`](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/GLM-5.3-w8a8c8) | 755.71B | ~764 GB | W8A8C8: INT8 weight (per-channel), INT8 activation (per-token dynamic), INT8 KV cache (per-tile 128) |
| `GLM-5.1-DevEco` | [`Eco-Tech/GLM-5.1-w4a8`](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/GLM-5.1-w4a8) | 395.82B | ~420 GB | W4A8 (the card does not expand the quantization recipe) |

- Both are Ascend deployments. GLM-5.3 uses msModelSlim + QuaRot and is validated with vLLM-Ascend on Atlas A2/A3; GLM-5.1 is validated on Atlas 800T A3 with vLLM-Ascend.
- Both ModelScope repositories are MIT-licensed. The base models keep their own licenses: GLM-5.3's original weights follow the ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3 repository terms, and GLM-5.1's base is `zai-org/GLM-5.1`.
- The cards do not declare a context or output limit for this channel. The 170,000 / 32,000 values in this README come from DevEco's `modelConfig`, not from the model cards.
- GLM-5.1's card reports GPQA 87.3 against 86.2 official; GLM-5.3's card leaves the precision and deployment sections "to be added".

> The channel currently declares **170,000 context / 32,000 max output** for both `GLM-5.1-DevEco` and `GLM-5.3-DevEco`. That is lower than the public Zhipu specs (5.1: 200K/131K, 5.3: 1M/131K); the static fallback and example config use the channel's numbers, and a larger `max_tokens` is clamped to 32K.

### Measured context limits (2026-09-17)

Measured with a **needle-in-haystack** probe: a random code buried ~30% into a long filler prompt and asked back verbatim. `usage.prompt_tokens` from the response is the authoritative upstream count; sizes start at ~2.5K tokens and grow ~1.25× per step.

| Model | Declared `context_window` | Measured pass | Measured reject | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | not declared (absent from the model list) | 1,042,769 tokens (~85 s) | 1,044,994 → `400 OverLimitRequestBody` | hard cap **1,044,480** tokens (≈1020K) |
| `GLM-5.3-DevEco` (upstream `GLM-5.3`) | 170,000 | 198,197 tokens (116 s) | 209,880 → `403 ModelServiceError` | effective **≈200K** |
| `GLM-5.1-DevEco` (upstream `GLM-5.1`) | 170,000 | 198,192 tokens (49 s) | 204,110 → `403 ModelServiceError` | effective **≈200K** |

- **`deepseek-v4-flash` enforces a hard cap** and names it in the error: `the prompt length 1044994 must less than the maximum input length 1044480`. Crossing the line is a plain `400`, so the boundary is crisp.
- **GLM-5.x reports no length error.** It answers `403 ModelServiceError` (`Built-in model service is currently overloaded` / `Full inference timed out`) after ~35 s — a fast rejection, not a genuine timeout. 198K passes consistently, 204K and above fails consistently, so ≈200K is an **observed** ceiling rather than a declared one. Leave headroom in practice (~190K for GLM-5.1-DevEco, ~180K for GLM-5.3-DevEco — the latter already takes 116 s at 198K).
- GLM tokenizes the same text more cheaply (~1.17 tokens/word vs deepseek's 1.23), yet its usable window is an order of magnitude smaller.
- **The proxy did not crash under this load**: 50+ calls with single request bodies of ~4 MB all returned normal HTTP responses; the only 5xx came from an upstream disconnect while two huge requests ran in parallel (`upstream fetch failed`), and the proxy answered `500` and kept serving.
- To reproduce: trust `usage.prompt_tokens`, start at 2K and grow ~1.25× per step until rejected; moving the needle toward the end (~90%) additionally checks that the tail is read in full.

### Hidden model `deepseek-v4-flash`

It appears neither in `GET /v2/models` nor in the upstream `modelConfig`. Clients that build their model list dynamically will not see it — pin the model name by hand. The proxy does not gate model names, and the upstream publishes no metadata for it (context, modalities, tiers). To enable it explicitly (opencode shown), add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
"provider": {
  "deveco": {
    "models": {
      "deepseek-v4-flash": {
        "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash (1M)",
        "limit": { "context": 1044480, "output": 32000 }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`context` is the measured hard cap above; `output` is not declared upstream, so 32000 (the GLM tier) is used as a starting point. Its reasoning arrives on `reasoning_content` natively — no flag needed, unlike GLM.

## Behavior details

### Vision routing (a vision fallback for text models)

`GLM-5.1-DevEco` / `GLM-5.3-DevEco` are text models, and an image in the request is rejected upstream (HTTP 403). The proxy has a built-in **transparent vision forward** — no opencode config needed:

- **Which models count as text-only is derived from the upstream config**: the proxy reads `input_modalities` from `modelConfig` and treats models declaring only `["text"]` as text models (cached with the model list for an hour). A model the upstream adds later is routed correctly without a code change; when the config is unavailable (cold start, offline, logged out) a built-in list (`GLM-5.1,GLM-5.3`, upstream ids) is used.
- When the requested model is text-only and **the latest user message contains an image**, the proxy forwards the turn to the vision model `Qwen3_5_397B_A17B_w8a8_single` and returns the response unchanged — the client notices nothing.
- On the next turn without new images it goes back to the original model; older images in the history are replaced with a `[image]` placeholder (the previous turn's textual conclusion stays in the history), so the text model can't hit the 403 again.
- When forwarding to the vision model, `tools` / `tool_choice` are removed — that model does not emit structured tool calls and describes images in text instead.
- The OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints both apply it, streaming and non-streaming alike.

The routing shows up in the logs:

```
-> POST no-stream model=GLM-5.1-DevEco → vision:Qwen3_5_397B_A17B_w8a8_single
```

### Session stability (no more "stops answering after a few rounds")

DevEco limits how many sessions an account may open in a short window (`UserSessionLimitExceeded`). The proxy keys the Chat-Id on the conversation's **first user message** by default, so a Claude Code system prompt that changes every turn (date, working directory, …) still reuses the same Chat-Id and never trips the new-session limit.

- Clients can pin a session explicitly with `x-session-id` / `x-deveco-session` / `x-session-affinity` headers (highest priority);
- to restore the old "system + first message" semantics, set `DEVECO_SESSION_KEY_MODE=system-first`.

### Concurrency and queueing

- `DEVECO_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default `1`) caps how many upstream generations may run at once, so a burst queues in arrival order instead of tripping DevEco's per-account throttle.
- A request that had to queue waits `DEVECO_QUEUE_COOLDOWN_SEC` (default `1`, fractions allowed; `0` switches it off) before admission; a request that finds a free slot starts immediately, and the cooling slot stays reserved for the waiter so a latecomer can't take it.
- The queue is bounded: at most `DEVECO_MAX_QUEUE` (default `3`) requests may wait; anything beyond is refused on the spot with `429` (`rate_limit_error`) instead of stacking up behind a long turn. `0` means "never queue".
- A finished turn's slot is passed to the next queued turn only once DevEco confirms the server-side queue slot is released (`exitSessionQueue`, capped at 3s). Metadata endpoints (`/v2/status`, `/v2/models`, `/v2/login`, `/v2/logout`) never queue at all.

### Configuration reference (environment variables)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DEVECO_PROXY_PORT` | `17128` | Proxy listen port; update the provider `baseURL` to match |
| `DEVECO_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | Log level: `debug` / `info` / `warn` / `error` |
| `DEVECO_VISION_MODEL` | `Qwen3_5_397B_A17B_w8a8_single` | Vision fallback model |
| `DEVECO_TEXT_ONLY_MODELS` | Automatic (from upstream `input_modalities`) | Comma-separated models treated as text-only; when set, takes precedence; falls back to the built-in `GLM-5.1,GLM-5.3` when the model config is unavailable |

## Token storage & refresh

| Credential | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `accessToken` (30 min) | in-memory in the proxy | auto-refreshed on the next request |
| `jwtToken` (long-lived refresh credential) | `~/.config/opencode/opencode-deveco/jwt.json` | plain JSON, `0600`; override dir with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` |
| country/region (not a credential) | `~/.config/deveco/country.region.xml` | written on a successful login for DevEco Studio; atomic write, failures only logged |

### Do I need to log in again when the token expires / after a reboot?

**No**, in almost all cases — browser login is only needed when the long-lived `jwtToken` itself expires (days/weeks). Three cases:

| Scenario | Re-login? | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| `accessToken` expires (every 30 min) | ❌ No | The proxy silently refreshes it with the stored jwtToken — no browser, no action. A second safety net: if DevEco returns `401` mid-request, the proxy refreshes once and retries. |
| Machine / proxy restart | ❌ No | On startup the proxy reads `jwt.json` and refreshes to restore the session headlessly (`GET /v2/status` → `logged_in:true`). You only need to **restart the proxy process**; consider adding it to your OS autostart. |
| `jwtToken` also expires | ⚠️ Yes | When the long-lived jwtToken is no longer valid server-side, refresh fails. The next request then auto-triggers browser login, or run `curl http://127.0.0.1:17128/v2/login` manually. |

On startup the proxy tries to restore a session from the stored jwtToken (refresh-on-boot). If that fails it waits for the next request to trigger browser login.

## Limitations

- **China site only.** Non-CN `siteId` values are rejected; non-China accounts are refused at login, and accounts without Huawei real-name verification are prompted to complete it before inference.
- **The 1.x proxy must keep running** for opencode 1.x to reach DevEco (its published binary doesn't load external plugin auth hooks). Run it as a background service / startup task. The 2.x plugin needs no proxy.
- **Plain-JSON jwtToken storage** (no encryption). Swap `JsonTokenStore` for an encrypted impl if needed — only `token-store.ts` changes.
- **One proxy instance per account.** A second process sharing the same `jwt.json` cannot refresh — DevEco appears to invalidate the previous refresh when another one succeeds — and it will fall back to a browser login.
- **Default port 17128** is not configurable via opencode; change it via `DEVECO_PROXY_PORT` and update the provider `baseURL`.

## Troubleshooting

- **`opencode run ... -m deveco/GLM-5.1-DevEco` fails with connection refused** → the proxy isn't running. Start it (`node dist/proxy.js`).
- **First request opens a browser and returns `401`** → that's expected when logged out: the proxy starts the login in the background rather than making you wait. Finish the Huawei login and retry; the next 30 minutes are headless.
- **`401` after a while** → access token expired and refresh failed (jwtToken no longer valid server-side). Hit `/v2/login` again.
- **A long turn ends with `Upstream stream ended early`** → DevEco went quiet for 120s mid-answer. Retry; if it repeats, the conversation is likely too large for the model's context and needs compacting.
- **`opencode models` shows no deveco models** → check the `provider.deveco` entry exists in `opencode.json` (this is config-driven, not plugin-driven).
- **Non-streaming requests time out** → DevEco's `/no-stream` endpoint can be slow; send `"stream": true` to opt back into streaming. The proxy defaults OpenAI requests to non-streaming (only an explicit `stream: true` enables SSE); opencode always sends `stream: true`, so it is unaffected.

## Recent improvements

Long Claude Code sessions used to break after a few rounds; the fixes for that and for login are the recent bulk of the work. `git log` has the reasoning behind each.

- **Session ids are normalized for the gateway** — ZCode sends a 36-character UUID in `x-session-id`; DevEco rejects a `Session-Id` longer than 32 characters. The proxy now compacts UUIDs (and hashes anything longer) to a 32-char id, so ZCode and opencode both work.
- **Models are exposed under DevEco-specific names** — the model list and injected catalog use `GLM-5.1-DevEco` / `GLM-5.3-DevEco`, making clear these are Huawei-deployed variants rather than public Zhipu models. The bare upstream ids are still accepted as aliases and stay on the wire.
- **Channel limits are visible and enforced** — `/v2/models` reports `context_length: 170000` and `max_output_tokens: 32000` for GLM-5.1-DevEco/5.3-DevEco. A larger `max_tokens` is clamped to 32K, and explicit over-limit upstream errors get a hint naming the channel limit. GLM's 403 `ModelServiceError` is left alone: it can mean overload as well as a length overflow.
- **Gateway headers follow the upstream contract** — inference and `exitSessionQueue` now send `x-deveco-session` / `x-deveco-task` / `x-deveco-client`; the same per-turn task id is used on both calls, and `x-deveco-project` / `x-deveco-parent-session` pass through when present. The legacy `Chat-Id` / `Session-Id` headers are kept for compatibility.
- **Vision fallback moved to the current model** — the old `Qwen3_VL_235B_A22B_Instruct` now rejects image requests with a 400 content-schema error. The fallback is now `Qwen3_5_397B_A17B_w8a8_single` (verified with a real image request).
- **Corporate proxies work** — `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` are honoured on every outgoing request (login, token refresh, model list, inference) through undici. `NO_PROXY` is respected; no extra setup behind a company proxy.
- **Improvement telemetry follows the official client** — `X-DevEco-Improvement-Enabled` is sent as `true` by default, matching the official 0.3.0 client; set `DEVECO_TOOL_IMPROVEMENT=0` to opt out.
- **Non-China accounts are refused at login** — a non-CN `nationalCode` fails the login with an actionable message, instead of a successful sign-in that breaks on the first turn.
- **Country/region file for DevEco Studio** — a successful login writes `~/.config/deveco/country.region.xml` (atomic write, Windows-sharing retry); a failed write is logged and never turns a successful login into a failed one.
- **Readable network failures** — DNS, proxy, TLS and connection failures now say what to check instead of surfacing a bare `fetch failed`.
- **Static fallback refreshed** — when the dynamic catalog cannot be fetched, the fallback list now includes `GLM-5.3-DevEco` alongside `GLM-5.1-DevEco`.
- **Idle-based upstream timeout** — a turn is cut only after DevEco goes *silent* for 120s, instead of a 60s cap on its total length that killed long conversations. Interrupted streams now emit a real Anthropic `error` event rather than truncating.
- **Forced tool choice works** — `tool_choice: {"type":"tool"}` used to fail the whole request; DevEco only accepts the enum form.
- **`max_tokens` is honoured** — it was silently dropped on the Anthropic path.
- **Stable Chat-Id per conversation** — keyed on the conversation's *first user message* (not `messages[0]`, which is the system prompt on the OpenAI wire format), so a volatile system prompt (current time, cwd, …) can't mint a new DevEco session every turn and trip the upstream session limit. Clients can pin a session explicitly with `x-session-id` / `x-deveco-session` / `x-session-affinity`, or opt into system-scoped keys with `DEVECO_SESSION_KEY_MODE=system-first`. The queue slot is released via `exitSessionQueue` when a turn ends.
- **Honest `logged_in`** — `/v2/status` reports `logged_in:true` as long as credentials exist and can be silently refreshed, not only while the current access token is unexpired (it expires every 30 minutes).
- **Client disconnects release the upstream** — a dropped SSE/HTTP client cancels the upstream read loop instead of draining the backend connection into a dead pipe, and a client that leaves while its request is still queued is dropped from the queue (no upstream turn at all, and no cooldown charged to the requests behind it); graceful shutdown no longer hangs on long-lived streams (5s grace, then force-close).
- **Reasoning no longer leaks into the answer** — DevEco's GLM models write their thinking into `content` (closed by a stray `</think>`, with no opening tag), so clients rendered the scratchpad as part of the reply. The proxy now asks the upstream to report reasoning on its own channel: `reasoning_content` on the OpenAI endpoint, a standard `thinking` block on the Anthropic one, with clean content either way. Assistant messages that still carry such a scratchpad are cleaned before forwarding, so pollution can't accumulate over turns. The thinking *level* is untouched — `reasoning_effort` (and the Anthropic thinking-budget mapping) passes through and still takes effect.
- **Reasoning tiers are switchable** — the tiers the cloud declares per model (`GLM-5.3-DevEco`: `low/high/max`, default `high`) become opencode model variants (`Ctrl+T`) on both paths (1.x and 2.x; the 2.x catalog prefers the persisted cloud catalog over its built-in fallback) and the declared default rides every request. A client tier outside that list is snapped onto the nearest declared one: measured, `GLM-5.3-DevEco` `medium` used to land on the *heaviest* tier (352 chars of reasoning against 103 for `high`) and now lands on `high`. A value the proxy cannot map at all (unknown vocabulary, a non-string, or an empty value) is dropped so the upstream default applies — it is never forwarded to the validator. A model that declares no tiers (`GLM-5.1-DevEco`) keeps the standard OpenAI tiers unchanged and still maps `none`/`off` to a disabled-thinking request.
- **Both paths are covered end-to-end, offline** — `npm run test:e2e` drives a real `opencode acp` process against a local mock upstream and asserts the whole normalisation contract on every chat turn (Bearer/headers, wire model id, `reasoning_effort`, `enable_thinking`, `max_tokens` clamp, `tool_choice` and role enums, no `developer` role); `npm run test:e2e:proxy` does the same for the 1.x local proxy with a real opencode 1.x binary, a scratch HOME and a seeded fake `jwt.json`. Neither needs a Huawei account.
- **The model list reaches opencode by itself** — a successful fetch is persisted (`<config>/opencode-deveco/models.json`, 0600, atomic write) and injected at startup, so the picker lists every cloud model with its context limit, tiers and modalities; models already written into `opencode.json` are merged (your fields win, cloud metadata fills the rest). `small_model` follows the cloud as well.
- **Text-only detection follows the upstream config** — which models need the vision fallback is derived from the upstream `input_modalities` (cached with the model list for an hour), so a model the upstream adds is routed correctly without a code change; a built-in list still covers cold starts.
- **Region and identity gates, as the official client** — a European timezone (including the Russian/Central-Asian zones the upstream groups with it) gets `451` with the official wording, a non-China account gets `403`, and an account without HUAWEI real-name verification is told to complete it instead of failing upstream; verified accounts pay nothing extra.
- **Refresh/logout race guards** — signing out invalidates a login exchange still in flight, so tokens can no longer be written back after a logout, and a refresh re-checks that the stored jwtToken has not changed.
- **Turns run one at a time** — `DEVECO_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default `1`) caps how many upstream generations may run at once, so a burst queues in arrival order instead of tripping DevEco's per-account throttle.
- **Queued requests can cool down** — `DEVECO_QUEUE_COOLDOWN_SEC` (default `1`, fractions allowed; `0` switches it off) pauses that many seconds before a request that had to queue is admitted, so burst-adjacent turns don't hit the backend back-to-back. A request that finds a free slot still starts immediately, and the cooling slot stays reserved for the waiter so a latecomer can't take it.
- **The queue is bounded** — at most `DEVECO_MAX_QUEUE` (default `3`) requests may wait for a slot; anything beyond that is refused on the spot with `429` (`rate_limit_error`) instead of stacking up behind a long turn, so a burst can't become an endless backlog. `0` means "never queue": no free slot, no waiting. A refused request takes no slot and doesn't disturb the waiters already queued.
- **Turns hand over cleanly** — a finished turn's slot is passed to the next queued turn only once DevEco confirms the server-side queue slot is released (`exitSessionQueue`), capped at 3s so a wedged release call can't stall the queue. Metadata endpoints (`/v2/status`, `/v2/models`, `/v2/login`, `/v2/logout`) never queue at all: they are reads, not generations.
- **Bounded request bodies** (128 MB) and `POST`-only chat forwarding.
- **Non-blocking login** — `/v2/login` redirects immediately, and requests made while logged out fail fast with the login URL instead of hanging.
- **Graceful shutdown**, **hourly model-list refresh**, **`fetch` everywhere** (the custom `HttpClient` is gone), **lint + tests**, and an optional `/v2` prefix on every endpoint.
